content.content:
Display pokemon sprites in your terminal.

Usage: pokeget [OPTIONS] [POKEMON]...

Arguments:
  [POKEMON]...  The pokemon to display, use "random" to get a random pokemon, use a region to get a random pokemon from that region

Options:
      --hide-name    Whether to hide the pokemon's name which appears above it
  -f, --form <FORM>  The form of the pokemon [default: ""]
  -m, --mega         Display the pokemon as it's mega form
      --mega-x       Display the pokemon as it's mega X form
      --mega-y       Display the pokemon as it's mega Y form
  -s, --shiny        Display the pokemon as shiny
  -a, --alolan       Display the alolan variant of the pokemon
  -g, --gmax         Display the gigantamax variant of the pokemon
      --hisui        Display the hisui variant of the pokemon
  -n, --noble        Display the noble variant of the pokemon, this option often times only works in tandom with --hisui
      --galar        Display the galarian variant of the pokemon
      --female       Display the female variant of the pokemon if it exists. This doesn't apply to nidoran, for some reason
  -h, --help         Print help
  -V, --version      Print version

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically centered
# alongside the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

pokeget --hide-name "$@" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad < 0 )); then
    pad=0
fi

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$sprite" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically centered
# alongside the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

pokeget --hide-name "$@" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad < 0 )); then
    pad=0
fi

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$sprite" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad"

lastPrompt: I have installed a tool called pokeget from https://github.com/talwat/pokeget-rs and I want to run it with fastfetch to make the pokemon figure be always centered on the left side of the text info in…

content.text:
Done. `pokefetch` is now installed at `~/.local/bin/pokefetch` (already on your `$PATH`) and works like this:

```
pokefetch pikachu          # any pokeget name/flags work
pokefetch charizard -s     # shiny charizard, etc.
pokefetch random
```

**How it works:** it generates the pokeget sprite to a temp file, measures its height, measures your fastfetch info-column height (using `~/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc`, the one of your existing configs without box borders — best fit for a side-by-side logo), computes the padding needed to center the shorter one, then calls `fastfetch --logo-type file-raw --logo <sprite> --logo-padding-top <N>`.

I verified it with both a short sprite (Pikachu, 10 lines) and a tall one (Charizard, 20 lines) — both come out vertically centered against the info block regardless of height.

Note: your `config.jsonc` (the default `fastfetch` config) already embeds a different tool, `pokemon-colorscripts`, as a stacked-on-top module — I left that untouched, so plain `fastfetch` still behaves exactly as before. `pokefetch` is a separate command that doesn't touch your existing setup.

If you want `pokefetch` to use a different fastfetch config (e.g. one with the box borders), set `POKEFETCH_CONFIG=/path/to/config.jsonc pokefetch pikachu`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically centered
# alongside the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

pokeget --hide-name "$@" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad < 0 )); then
    pad=0
fi

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$sprite" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically centered
# alongside the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). When pokefetch
# is called with no arguments, one entry is picked at random. Passing
# your own arguments (e.g. `pokefetch bulbasaur -s`) always overrides
# this list.
FAVORITES=(
    "pikachu"
    "charizard -s"
    "gengar"
    "lucario"
    "greninja -s"
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

if [[ $# -eq 0 && ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically centered
# alongside the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

pokeget --hide-name "$@" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad < 0 )); then
    pad=0
fi

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$sprite" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically centered
     3	# alongside the system info column.
     4	set -euo pipefail
     5	
     6	# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
     7	# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
     8	# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). When pokefetch
     9	# is called with no arguments, one entry is picked at random. Passing
    10	# your own arguments (e.g. `pokefetch bulbasaur -s`) always overrides
    11	# this list.
    12	FAVORITES=(
    13	)
    14	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    15	
    16	FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"
    17	
    18	sprite="$(mktemp)"
    19	trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT
    20	
    21	if [[ $# -eq 0 && ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    22	    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    23	    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
    24	else
    25	    args=("$@")
    26	fi
    27	
    28	pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"
    29	
    30	sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
    31	info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)
    32	
    33	pad=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
    34	if (( pad < 0 )); then
    35	    pad=0
    36	fi
    37	
    38	fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    39	    --logo-type file-raw \
    40	    --logo "$sprite" \
    41	    --logo-padding-top "$pad"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Assumed max sprite width (terminal columns), used to horizontally
# center narrower sprites within a consistent column. Bump this up if
# you use a pokemon/form wider than this (e.g. mega/gmax forms).
TARGET_WIDTH=44
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Assumed max sprite width (terminal columns), used to horizontally
# center narrower sprites within a consistent column. Bump this up if
# you use a pokemon/form wider than this (e.g. mega/gmax forms).
TARGET_WIDTH=44
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (TARGET_WIDTH - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$sprite" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    --logo-padding-left "$pad_left"

2	# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
3	# horizontally centered against the system info column.
4	set -euo pipefail
5	
6	# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
7	# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
8	#          script are ignored)
9	# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
10	USE_FAVORITES=true
11	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
12	
13	# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
14	# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
15	# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
16	# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
17	FAVORITES=(
18	)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
     3	# horizontally centered against the system info column.
     4	set -euo pipefail
     5	
     6	# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
     7	# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
     8	#          script are ignored)
     9	# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
    10	USE_FAVORITES=false
    11	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    12	
    13	# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
    14	# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
    15	# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
    16	# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
    17	FAVORITES=(
    18	)
    19	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    20	
    21	# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
    22	# Assumed max sprite width (terminal columns), used to horizontally
    23	# center narrower sprites within a consistent column. Bump this up if
    24	# you use a pokemon/form wider than this (e.g. mega/gmax forms).
    25	TARGET_WIDTH=44
    26	# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
    27	
    28	FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"
    29	
    30	sprite="$(mktemp)"
    31	trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT
    32	
    33	if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    34	    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    35	    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
    36	else
    37	    args=("$@")
    38	fi
    39	
    40	pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"
    41	
    42	sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
    43	sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
    44	info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)
    45	
    46	pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
    47	if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    48	    pad_top=0
    49	fi
    50	
    51	pad_left=$(( (TARGET_WIDTH - sprite_width) / 2 ))
    52	if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    53	    pad_left=0
    54	fi
    55	
    56	fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    57	    --logo-type file-raw \
    58	    --logo "$sprite" \
    59	    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    60	    --logo-padding-left "$pad_left"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Assumed max sprite width (terminal columns), used to horizontally
# center narrower sprites within a consistent column. Bump this up if
# you use a pokemon/form wider than this (e.g. mega/gmax forms).
TARGET_WIDTH=44
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (TARGET_WIDTH - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$sprite" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    --logo-padding-left "$pad_left"

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Fixed width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Bump this up if you use a pokemon/form wider than this (e.g. mega/gmax
# forms) - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=44
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (POKEMON_WIDTH - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly POKEMON_WIDTH visible columns wide, regardless of the shape
# of that particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$POKEMON_WIDTH" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)

TARGET_WIDTH=44

sprite="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (TARGET_WIDTH - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$sprite" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top" \
    --logo-padding-left "$pad_left"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Fixed width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Bump this up if you use a pokemon/form wider than this (e.g. mega/gmax
# forms) - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=44
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (POKEMON_WIDTH - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly POKEMON_WIDTH visible columns wide, regardless of the shape
# of that particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$POKEMON_WIDTH" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the sprite's own height (in rows) each run;
# set a fixed number here instead if you want a constant width no
# matter which pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's
# left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$sprite_lines}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run; set a fixed number here instead if you want a
# constant width no matter which pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is
# wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$sprite_lines}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

lines: sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)

# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run; set a fixed number here instead if you want a
# constant width no matter which pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is
# wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$sprite_lines}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.

{

    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}

SCRATCH=/tmp/claude-1000/-home-krubics/c67dfedc-12d6-4890-b891-1f30e3c5ab6b/scratchpad
sprite="$SCRATCH/pika.txt"
width=24
pad_left=1
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$SCRATCH/pika_padded.txt"
sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$SCRATCH/pika_padded.txt" | awk '{print length}'

options.label: There's a fixed ~4-col gap fastfetch adds after the logo
options.description: fastfetch itself inserts its own built-in spacing between the logo column and the info column (confirmed: a 4-char logo renders with 4 extra trailing spaces before info text starts). options.description: Maybe using the full output's line count (e.g. 24) makes narrow sprites look stretched/oddly spaced since terminal characters aren't square. You want a formula that accounts for character aspect ratio instead of a raw 1:1 row-count.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run; set a fixed number here instead if you want a
# constant width no matter which pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is
# wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$info_lines}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run; set a fixed number here instead if you want a
# constant width no matter which pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is
# wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$info_lines}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------

USE_FAVORITES=false

# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run; set a fixed number here instead if you want a
# constant width no matter which pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is
# wider than this, it's left as-is (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$info_lines}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))

    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run fastfetch with a pokeget sprite as the logo, vertically and
# horizontally centered against the system info column.
set -euo pipefail

# --- Mode switch ----------------------------------------------------------
# true  -> always draw a random entry from FAVORITES below (args to this
#          script are ignored)
# false -> forward "$@" straight through to pokeget as-is
USE_FAVORITES=false
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Favourites -------------------------------------------------------
# Each entry is anything pokeget itself accepts: a name, "random", a
# region, plus any flags (-s, -m, --shiny, --gmax, etc). Only used when
# USE_FAVORITES=true above; one entry is picked at random per run.
FAVORITES=(
)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Sizing -----------------------------------------------------------
# Width (terminal columns) of the pokemon column. Every sprite is
# centered and padded out to exactly this width, so the info column
# always starts at the same spot no matter which pokemon is drawn.
# Leave empty to default to the height of the whole fastfetch output
# (in rows) each run, scaled by CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO below; set a fixed
# number here instead if you want a constant width no matter which
# pokemon is drawn - if a sprite is wider than this, it's left as-is
# (uncentered).
POKEMON_WIDTH=

# Terminal character cells are taller than they are wide (commonly
# ~2x), so N rows need roughly N * CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO columns to look
# square. Only used to compute the default width above; tweak this to
# match your terminal font if the result looks too narrow/wide.
CHAR_ASPECT_RATIO=2
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------

FASTFETCH_CONFIG="${POKEFETCH_CONFIG:-$HOME/.config/fastfetch/normal.jsonc}"

sprite="$(mktemp)"
padded="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "$sprite" "$padded"' EXIT

if $USE_FAVORITES && [[ ${#FAVORITES[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
    chosen="${FAVORITES[RANDOM % ${#FAVORITES[@]}]}"
    read -r -a args <<< "$chosen"
else
    args=("$@")
fi

pokeget --hide-name "${args[@]}" > "$sprite"

sprite_lines=$(wc -l < "$sprite")
sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
info_lines=$(fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" --logo none | wc -l)

width="${POKEMON_WIDTH:-$info_lines}"

pad_top=$(( (info_lines - sprite_lines) / 2 ))
if (( pad_top < 0 )); then
    pad_top=0
fi

pad_left=$(( (width - sprite_width) / 2 ))
if (( pad_left < 0 )); then
    pad_left=0
fi

# Left-pad every line by the same amount (keeps the sprite's shape
# intact) and right-pad each line individually so every line ends up
# exactly $width visible columns wide, regardless of the shape of that
# particular row.
awk -v padleft="$pad_left" -v width="$width" '
{
    stripped = $0
    gsub(/\033\[[0-9;]*m/, "", stripped)
    rightpad = width - padleft - length(stripped)
    if (rightpad < 0) rightpad = 0
    printf "%s%s%s\n", sprintf("%*s", padleft, ""), $0, sprintf("%*s", rightpad, "")
}
' "$sprite" > "$padded"

fastfetch -c "$FASTFETCH_CONFIG" \
    --logo-type file-raw \
    --logo "$padded" \
    --logo-padding-top "$pad_top"

lines: sprite_width=$(sed 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g' "$sprite" | awk '{ print length }' | sort -n | tail -1)
